verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both equalities are stated, as a chain of four theorems rather than one. The scaling step is physical_moment_scaling: the Lean exponent is q^{1-h} where the paper writes q^{3/2-A}, and these are the same number, since A = 1/2 + h (RenormalizedHeatMoment.A h = 1/2 + h, line 191 context; StressAlgebra.velocityExponent h = 1/2 + h), so 3/2 - A = 1 - h exactly. The left-hand integrand matches: renormalizedMoment u ref z = ∫_0^∞ r²(u(z,r) - ref r) (line 109) with ref = referencePower h C r = C·(r²/2)^{-A h} (line 191), the power tail K_pow. The change of variable to X = r²/2 is profileMoment_eq_xMoment together with xMoment_eq_outgoing_reference, whose right-hand side is ∫_0^∞ (H - H_pow) dX with H = √(2X)·E (HeatedOutgoing.lean:39) and H_pow = √(2X)·powerE (OutgoingDilation.lean:67). The vanishing is CompensationWitness.renormalized_zero. Composing the four gives (A.45) verbatim; the only differences are packaging and the use of 1 - h for 3/2 - A. The Lean statement is for η in the parameter domain, whereas the paper's display suppresses η.
